question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-h,5h],$ where $h$ is a positive number, compute $P(0<X\le 3h).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-h,5h],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6h},\, & -h\le x\le 5h, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 3h) & ={\int }_{0}^{3h}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3h}\frac{1}{6h}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3h-0}{6h} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
